title: Humanoid robot rental prices crater as dedicated exchanges appear
source_used: Notebookcheck (read in full from the pre-fetched text; page date 10 Oct 2026)
key_facts: After Unitree's robots danced on China's 2025 Spring Festival Gala, demand for humanoid rentals surged and daily rates reportedly reached five figures in yuan, roughly $1,400 or more.
The 'newest report' (not named) shows rates fell to about 2,000 to 3,000 yuan a day ($280 to $420) by early 2026 and have since slipped below 1,000 yuan.
On one classifieds marketplace some merchants list Unitree humanoids from 289 yuan a day, roughly $40.
Reasons given: more machines in circulation and a fading novelty premium; the 2026 gala put four robot makers on stage.
Qingtianzu, billed as the world's first dedicated robot rental platform, announced a seed round in January 2026; its order volume reportedly grew about 30 percent in the first week of February.
The article suggests rentals are mostly a cheap way to try a humanoid and often serve as showpieces at festivals and exhibitions while the robots sit idle.
A Unitree G1+ costs from 95,000 yuan (about $13,000) to buy; China has over 70 robot training facilities with more than 40 under construction.
quote_evidence: That bubble has now deflated as the newest report shows that rates fell to around 2,000 to 3,000 yuan per day (about $280 to $420) by early 2026.
On one classifieds marketplace, some merchants now list Unitree humanoids from just 289 yuan per day, or roughly $40.
In January 2026, Qingtianzu, billed as the world's first dedicated robot rental platform, announced a seed round.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheaper rentals make it easier for businesses and curious customers to try humanoid robots, though many rentals are for shows.
event_date: Price figures refer to early 2026 and later; Notebookcheck page dated 10 Oct 2026
notes: Notebookcheck cites an unnamed 'newest report'; several data points (early 2026 prices, January and February 2026 events) are older than the article date. The prices are from rental listings and reports, not an official survey. Page date 10 Oct 2026 confirmed from the page metadata, so not held as old news.
